issues.description: coerceNumber silently changes toNumber semantics by mapping null to 0 instead of propagating NaN.
issues.detail: Original panLinear used toNumber as lift, which returns null for non-numeric input and propagates NaN through arithmetic. The new coerceNumber coerces null to 0, changing observable output for bad input. This is a runtime behavior change buried in a 'just types' PR. Either preserve NaN propagation or document the new mapping in release notes.

issues.description: Public contract strengthened: empty-domain inputs now throw instead of soft-failing to NaN/undefined.
issues.detail: The prior implementation tolerated empty arrays (peek returned undefined, arithmetic yielded NaN). The new implementation throws, strengthening the precondition of a published API. Any caller relying on soft-fail behavior breaks. Document the change in release notes and the type signature, or make it non-throwing for backwards compatibility.

issues.description: Domain parameter typed as number[] when the body requires NonEmptyArray<number>.
issues.detail: The functions require non-empty domains at runtime but advertise number[] in the type signature. Since peek now has a non-empty overload, pan/zoom should accept NonEmptyArray<number> (or readonly [number, ...number[]]) so the type system enforces what the body asserts. Half-typed is worse than fully typed — the abstraction leaks.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the isNonEmpty guard runs, with no test coverage for Log/Pow/Symlog empty-domain paths.
issues.detail: panLog and zoomLog call Math.sign(domain[0]) before delegating to pan/zoom, so an empty domain reads undefined and yields sign=NaN before the error is thrown. The error still fires inside pan, but the order is sloppy and the new test only covers Linear. Either guard at the public entry points or add tests for the Log/Pow/Symlog variants.

issues.description: Domain return type [number, number] under-specifies invariants like ordering and finiteness.
issues.detail: A domain typically carries invariants beyond 'tuple of two numbers' — d0 <= d1, or both finite. The new Domain type captures arity but not these invariants. Acceptable for an incremental typing PR, but worth a follow-up so callers cannot accidentally consume a [NaN, NaN] result as a valid domain.

issues.description: Local identity TransformFn shadows the existing accessors.identity import previously used.
issues.detail: The old file imported identity from './accessors.js'. The new file defines a local identity: TransformFn = x => x and drops the import. Functionally equivalent for numbers, but diverges from codebase voice and duplicates an existing utility. Either keep the import or justify the narrower-typed local in a comment.

synthesis.summary: The PR ports transform.js to TypeScript and adds an empty-domain guard, with peek getting a clean non-empty overload refinement. Two contract changes slip in under the 'types only' banner: coerceNumber maps null to 0 instead of propagating NaN like toNumber did, and empty domains now throw instead of soft-failing. Both are observable behavior changes at a published API boundary and need to be documented or reverted. The parameter types should also reflect the non-empty invariant the body enforces, and the Log/Pow/Symlog variants need test coverage matching Linear's. NEEDS-WORK.
